subject: Request: Temporary SLO waiver for Nimbus preview model v0.9
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Lin <avery.lin@nimbus.health>, Katrina Soto <katrina@nimbus.health>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Temporary SLO waiver for Nimbus preview model v0.9

Hi Avery / Katrina —

Thanks again for the test-run this week. As we discussed on the call, the v0.9 preview model provides markedly better clinical extraction for your workflows but has a longer 95th percentile token latency under real patient payloads. For the pilot launch next week we need to formally document a temporary SLO waiver for the preview route while we push kernel/quantization improvements.

Proposed ask to Nimbus: 2-week temporary SLO waiver for 95th percentile latency from 800ms -> 1.6s on the preview route, with the following constraints:
- Waiver window: 2026-12-09 to 2026-12-23
- Fallback: requests exceeding 2.0s will be auto-routed to the GA model variant
- Observability: Redwood will provide daily latency dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns
- Rollback: We will pause the preview route if error rate increases >0.5% or if latency >2.0s for more than 25% of 5-minute windows

I'm copying Dev, Neha and Marissa to call out operational and security guardrails. I've attached an SLO matrix and the current latency traces for the preview run. Please confirm if Nimbus can accept a temporary, documented waiver with those rollback conditions.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0179

Attachments: nimbus_preview_slo_matrix.xlsx, ga4_latency_traces.zip

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary SLO waiver for Nimbus preview model v0.9

Ben / team —

Quick security/compliance input: before we sign off on any formal waiver we need:
1) Written acknowledgement from Nimbus that preview data will not be used for training outside the agreed retention window
2) Access controls for debug traces (PII redaction confirmed)
3) Audit log export schedule for the waiver period

Dev — can you confirm how debug traces are redacted in this preview and whether the audit export can be delivered daily? Marissa — need to confirm whether we can auto-enable the GA fallback without creating additional audit noise.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary SLO waiver for Nimbus preview model v0.9

Neha —

Notes from engineering:
- Preview traces have PII redaction enabled at the proxy layer; any flagged PHI is masked before hitting our observability pipeline. I attached the latency traces we captured in staging (ga4_latency_traces.zip).
- We can add a per-customer audit export daily to a customer-owned S3 bucket (requires a quick IAM consent from Nimbus)
- Automatic fallback to GA variant is implemented as a routing rule; enabling it does not increase error rates we observed in testing.

Open items:
- We need Nimbus ops to confirm they can accept the 2.0s hard cap before we flip routing live.
- There will be a ~4 hour maintenance window to push the kernel patches that are expected to reduce 95p latency by ~25% — we propose scheduling that during your low-traffic window (Sun 12/12).

Happy to run through the trace files with Nimbus if helpful.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Avery Lin <avery.lin@nimbus.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Katrina Soto <katrina@nimbus.health>, procurement@nimbus.health
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary SLO waiver for Nimbus preview model v0.9

Hi Ben / Dev —

Thanks for the clear proposal. From Nimbus ops side:
- We can accept a temporary 95p latency increase to 1.6s for two weeks, provided:
  * We receive a daily latency dashboard and a daily audit export to our S3 bucket at s3://nimbus-ops-preview-exports (IAM consent to follow)
  * There is an explicit rollback trigger if any 5-minute window has >1% error rate
- We need confirmation that the fallback to GA variant will preserve request ordering for transactional writes (this is critical for our ingestion pipeline)

Can you add a short mutual action plan with exact handoffs so procurement can expedite a one-time addendum?

Best,
Avery
Avery Lin
Product Operations Manager, Nimbus Health
avery.lin@nimbus.health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Avery Lin <avery.lin@nimbus.health>, Katrina Soto <katrina@nimbus.health>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary SLO waiver for Nimbus preview model v0.9

Thanks — putting together a concise mutual action plan below (can paste into procurement addendum):

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Dates: 2026-12-09 -> 2026-12-23 (adjustable if both parties agree)
- Objectives: Allow Nimbus to test preview model v0.9 in production traffic while Redwood iterates kernel/quantization improvements
- Redwood deliverables:
  1) Daily latency dashboard (shared Drive link + CSV export by 08:00 PT)
  2) Daily audit export to s3://nimbus-ops-preview-exports (customer-owned bucket; IAM consent required)
  3) Auto-fallback routing rule: threshold 2.0s; hard rollback on 25% violated windows or >0.5% sustained error rate
  4) One scheduled maintenance window on Sun 12/12 (4 hours) to deploy improvements
- Nimbus deliverables:
  1) Provide IAM consent for S3 export by 2026-12-08 17:00 PT
  2) Confirm acceptance of GA fallback semantics for transactional ordering
  3) Procurement: sign addendum to accept temporary SLO variation
- Escalation path: Redwood Success ops (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) -> Ben Carter -> Redwood Head of Ops

I will create the procurement addendum draft and share a DocuSign link once IAM is confirmed.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Lin <avery.lin@nimbus.health>, Katrina Soto <katrina@nimbus.health>, procurement@nimbus.health
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary SLO waiver for Nimbus preview model v0.9

Avery / Katrina / Procurement —

Thank you — Nimbus's acceptance of the two-week window is noted. Next steps from Redwood:
1) Marissa will share the procurement addendum and DocuSign link by EOD 2026-12-08 once IAM details are confirmed.
2) Dev will enable daily audit exports as soon as we receive IAM consent; expect first export 2026-12-10 08:00 PT.
3) Neha: security sign-off is contingent on receipt of explicit written consent on data usage and confirmation of redaction settings (Avery, please confirm in reply).

Ben (on behalf of Redwood) requests a formal, one-paragraph confirmation from Nimbus accepting the temporary SLO boundaries and rollback triggers so we can file the waiver in our compliance tracker. Sample language below — feel free to paste and return: 

"Nimbus Health accepts a temporary change to the 95th percentile latency SLO for preview route v0.9 from 800ms to 1.6s between 2026-12-09 and 2026-12-23. Nimbus agrees to the rollback triggers and daily audit export requirements outlined by Redwood and will provide IAM consent for S3 exports.
"

Appreciate the quick turn here.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
